info.title: Kizuki local HTTP API
info.description:
Everything the Kizuki dashboard answers over HTTP. Kizuki runs on your computer and listens
only on `127.0.0.1`, so this reference is for reading how the app works, for testing, and
for tools you run on the same computer. No server on the internet hosts it.

Most addresses are pages that return HTML. Changes to your data go through **form
actions**: a page's forms post back to that page's address, and Next.js picks the action
from the `Next-Action` header. The action ids come from each build, so treat them as part
of the page, not as a stable API. The only other data address is `GET /files/{materialId}`,
which returns a file you added.

There is no login. Every address except the built files under `/_next/` checks the `Host`
header and refuses any name other than this computer (see the Host parameter). Every
answer carries the four safety headers listed under each response.

Next.js also answers `HEAD` for every page and file, with the same headers and no body, and
`OPTIONS` for route handlers. Addresses Kizuki has no page for get the 404 "Not found"
page.

## Requests Kizuki sends

Kizuki itself calls out only to the model servers in your settings (`baseURL`):

- **POST {baseURL}/embeddings**: Turns texts into numbers for meaning search, through the AI SDK: the passages of a file when it is added (32 at a time) or the search file is rebuilt, and your explanation and answers when a session looks for related passages. For nomic models each text starts with `search_document: ` or `search_query: `. Headers: `Authorization`: `Bearer <key>`, only when settings name an API key variable (`apiKeyEnv`).
- **POST {baseURL}/chat/completions**: Asks the answer model, through the AI SDK, to propose concepts, prerequisite links, or questions, or to list what you missed. The body holds Kizuki's instructions, the labeled sentences of your material, your corrections and readings, and (in a session) your explanation and answers. Temperature is 0.2. With reasoning `none` it adds `reasoning_effort: "none"` and `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`; with reply shape `server` it adds a `response_format` with the reply's JSON Schema. Headers: `Authorization`: `Bearer <key>`, only when settings name an API key variable (`apiKeyEnv`).
- **GET {baseURL}/models**: Lists the models a server has, to check that the answer model and the meaning-search model are installed. Sent once per server address each time the Today or Settings page loads, and by the `kizuki` command at start. Gives up after 5 seconds. Carries no study data. Headers: `Authorization`: `Bearer <key>`, only when settings name an API key variable (`apiKeyEnv`). The key is read from that environment variable.

tags.name: Pages
tags.description: The dashboard's pages. Each reads your data fresh from the logs on every request and returns HTML.

tags.name: Form actions
tags.description: The forms on each page. The browser posts them back to the page's own address, and each one changes your data through the checked commands in lib/, then sends the browser to the next page.

tags.name: Files
tags.description: The copies of the files you added.

tags.name: Background jobs
tags.description: Addresses the Workflow SDK adds for Kizuki's background jobs (reading a file, running a session). Kizuki's own job queue calls them on this computer; you never need to.

tags.name: Static files
tags.description: Pictures and built scripts that never change while Kizuki runs.

parameters.name: note
parameters.description: The id of a message a form action left for this page, such as "Settings saved." or an error. Only ids this running Kizuki made show anything; any other value is ignored.

200.description: The page.

500.description: Kizuki could not read your data, for example because a log line is broken. The page shows "Something went wrong"; the full message, with the file and line, is printed where Kizuki runs.

get.description:
The Today page: concepts due now, coming up, and waiting on others, and this week's catches.

Also checks that both models answer, and lists the problems if not.

post.description:
The forms on this page post here. The React code in the page sends the form as `multipart/form-data` with the action's id in the `Next-Action` header, and adds values the page bound when it rendered the form (such as the course id). With JavaScript on, React puts a prefix such as `_1_` before each field name. Without JavaScript, the browser posts the form itself, with the action id in a field named `$ACTION_ID_<id>`, and gets a 303 answer instead of a 200. Every action ends by sending the browser to a page: on success the next page, on an error the same page with a `note` id that shows the message. The body may be up to 200 MB (`serverActions.bodySizeLimit` in next.config.ts).

Forms on this page run: `createCourseAction`.

parameters.name: Next-Action
parameters.description: The id of the action to run. Next.js makes the ids when it builds the app, so they change with every build. Sent by React when JavaScript is on.

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: Set by the browser. Next.js refuses to run an action when Origin names a different host from the Host header, so another site's page cannot post Kizuki's forms.

200.description: The action ran (JavaScript on). The body is React's page data, and the browser then opens the address in `x-action-redirect`.

x-action-redirect.description: Where the browser goes next, followed by `;push`, as in `/courses/course_…;push` or, after an error, `/courses?note=…;push`.

303.description: The action ran (form posted without JavaScript). The browser goes to the next page.

location.description: The next page, as for `x-action-redirect` but without `;push`.

404.description: The action id is not one this build knows. The body is `Server action not found.`

500.description: Next.js refused to run the action because Origin names a different host from Host.

schema.title: createCourseAction
schema.description:
Creates a course and opens it.

**Result:** Opens the new course at `/courses/{courseId}`. On an error, goes to `/courses` with the message.

name.description: The course name. It must differ from your other courses' names, ignoring letter case.

get.description: Next.js answers here to resize pictures for pages that ask for it. Kizuki's pages never do. Its only picture is an SVG, which the resizer refuses, and it refuses addresses on other sites, so in Kizuki this answers 400. The host check does not run here.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The picture to resize.

parameters.name: w
parameters.description: The width in pixels.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The quality from 1 to 100.

400.description: A plain-text reason, such as `"url" parameter is required`, `"url" parameter is not allowed`, or `The requested resource isn't a valid image.`

get.description: The JavaScript and CSS files that `next build` made for the pages. Their names change with every build. The host check does not run on these addresses, because they hold no study data.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The file's path under `.next/static/`, such as `chunks/abc123.css`. It may contain slashes.

200.description: The file, with a content type that matches its ending.

404.description: No built file has this path.

get.description: Kizuki's job queue posts here to move a workflow (processing a file, or running a teach-back session) to its next step. The request and answer formats belong to the Workflow SDK and can change with its version. With `?__health` in the address, it answers whether the endpoint works instead.

parameters.name: __health
parameters.description: Present (with any value, or none) to ask for a health check.

200.description: The health check answer, such as `{"healthy":true,"endpoint":"/.well-known/workflow/v1/flow"}`, or the result of a queue message.

400.description: No request body, as in `{"error":"Missing request body"}`, or a body the SDK cannot read.

anyOf.title: dropConceptAction
anyOf.description:
Drops a concept.

**Result:** Back to the page in `back`.

**Set by the page:** `conceptId`, `back`

anyOf.title: renameConceptAction
anyOf.description:
Renames a concept.

**Result:** Back to the page in `back`.

**Set by the page:** `conceptId`, `back`

name.description: The new name: 1 to 120 characters, not used by another proposed or confirmed concept in the course.

anyOf.title: mergeConceptAction
anyOf.description:
Merges a concept into another one.

**Result:** Back to the page in `back`.

**Set by the page:** `conceptId`, `back`

into.description: The id of the concept to merge into. It must be in the same course, and the merge must not make a loop in the confirmed order.

anyOf.title: startSessionAction
anyOf.description:
Starts a teach-back session with your explanation.

**Result:** Starts the session and its background run, then opens `/sessions/{sessionId}`. On an error, back to the concept.

**Set by the page:** `conceptId`

explanation.description: Your explanation of the concept, in your own words. Required.

anyOf.title: abandonSessionAction
anyOf.description:
Stops an open session so a new one can start.

**Result:** Marks the session as stopped ("You stopped this session."), then opens the concept page so you can start again.

**Set by the page:** `sessionId`, `conceptId`

anyOf.title: setExamDateAction
anyOf.description:
Sets or clears a course's exam date.

**Result:** Back to the course.

**Set by the page:** `courseId`

examDate.description: The exam date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or empty to clear it.

anyOf.title: uploadAction
anyOf.description:
Adds uploaded files to a course and starts processing each one.

**Result:** Back to the course. Each file is copied into the data folder and its processing starts in the background. A file Kizuki can't read, or one already in the course, is named in the error message; the other files are still added.

**Set by the page:** `courseId`

files.description: One or more files; repeat the field for each. Kizuki reads `.pdf`, `.pptx`, `.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.csv`, `.md`, `.markdown`, and `.txt`. Empty entries are skipped. The whole request may be up to 200 MB.

anyOf.title: retryMaterialAction
anyOf.description:
Starts processing a file again after it failed.

**Result:** Starts processing the file again, then back to the course.

**Set by the page:** `courseId`, `materialId`

anyOf.title: doneReviewingAction
anyOf.description:
Tells a file's workflow you finished reviewing its concepts, so it goes on to suggest links.

**Result:** Tells the file's paused workflow that you finished reviewing its concepts, waits up to 15 seconds for the file to leave review, then back to the course. If that workflow is gone (for example after a restart), Kizuki records the review and asks the model for links itself.

**Set by the page:** `courseId`, `materialId`

get.description: Returns the copy of a file you added, byte for byte, from `files/` in the data folder. Source pages link here, with `#page=N` added for a PDF so the browser opens it at the quoted page.

parameters.name: materialId
parameters.description: The file's id, as in `mat_` followed by 16 letters and digits.

200.description: The file.

content-type.description: Set from the file's format: `application/pdf`; the Office types for pptx, docx, and xlsx (`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.…`); or `text/csv`, `text/markdown`, or `text/plain`, each with `; charset=utf-8`.

content-disposition.description: `inline` for PDF, markdown, text, and CSV, which a browser can show in a tab, and `attachment` for slides, documents, and workbooks, which download. Both carry the file's original name as `filename*=UTF-8''<name>`, with the name percent-encoded.

404.description: No file has this id. The body is the text `Not found`.

500.description: The copy is missing from `files/`, or the log line for the file was changed so that it points outside `files/` (`storedFilePath` in lib/paths.ts refuses it).

200.description: The page.

500.description: Kizuki could not read your data, for example because a log line is broken. The page shows "Something went wrong"; the full message, with the file and line, is printed where Kizuki runs.

anyOf.title: answerRoundAction
anyOf.description:
Sends your answers to one round of questions.

**Result:** Sends the answers to the session's paused run, waits up to 15 seconds for them to be saved, then back to the session. If the run is gone, Kizuki starts a new run that skips finished steps and sends the answers again.

**Set by the page:** `sessionId`, `round`

answer:{questionId}.description: Your answer to one question. May be empty.

verdict:{questionId}.description: For a "Does this fit?" question, required: `material-right` (you got it wrong), `material-wrong` (the material is wrong), or `misread` (Kizuki misread you).

correction:{questionId}.description: Your version, required when the verdict is `material-wrong`. It is saved as a correction.

finish.description: `yes` to stop asking after this round. Any other value asks for another round, up to three.

anyOf.title: finishReviewAction
anyOf.description:
Sends which proposed misses you confirm, which ends the session.

**Result:** Sends your choice to the session's paused run, which ends the session, waits up to 15 seconds, then back to the session.

**Set by the page:** `sessionId`

missed.description: The id of a proposed miss you missed; repeat the field for each. Leave it out if you missed none.

anyOf.title: restartSessionAction
anyOf.description:
Starts a new run for a session that stopped making progress. Finished steps are skipped.

**Result:** Starts a new run for the session (finished steps are skipped), then back to the session.

**Set by the page:** `sessionId`

anyOf.title: recordCatchAction
anyOf.description:
Records a catch for a finished session.

**Result:** Back to the session with "Catch recorded." Refused if the session has not ended.

**Set by the page:** `sessionId`

note.description: What you would have gotten wrong. May be empty.

schema.title: addCorrectionAction
schema.description:
Records your correction to a passage. The wrong text must appear in the passage word for word.

**Result:** Back to the passage with "Correction saved. Your version wins from now on."

**Set by the page:** `passageId`

quote.description: The wrong text, copied from the passage. It must pass the word-for-word quote check against the passage.

note.description: Optional: where the correction comes from, such as a lecture date.

X-Frame-Options.description: Always `DENY`. No other site may show Kizuki inside a frame, where it could trick you into a click.

Content-Security-Policy.description: Always `frame-ancestors 'none'`, the same rule as X-Frame-Options for newer browsers.

X-Content-Type-Options.description: Always `nosniff`. Browsers must use the content type Kizuki sends and never guess another.

Referrer-Policy.description: Always `no-referrer`. When you follow a link out of Kizuki, the other site is not told which Kizuki page you came from.

Host.name: Host
Host.description: Must name this computer: `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, or `[::1]`, with any port. Browsers and HTTP tools set it from the address you open. Any other name, or no Host header at all, gets the 403 answer. This stops a website that points its own domain name at your computer from reaching Kizuki, which has no login.

NotThisComputer.description: The Host header does not name this computer (see the Host parameter).

schema.const: Kizuki only answers requests addressed to this computer.

POST {baseURL}/embeddings.description: Turns texts into numbers for meaning search, through the AI SDK: the passages of a file when it is added (32 at a time) or the search file is rebuilt, and your explanation and answers when a session looks for related passages. For nomic models each text starts with `search_document: ` or `search_query: `.

headers.Authorization: `Bearer <key>`, only when settings name an API key variable (`apiKeyEnv`).

POST {baseURL}/chat/completions.description: Asks the answer model, through the AI SDK, to propose concepts, prerequisite links, or questions, or to list what you missed. The body holds Kizuki's instructions, the labeled sentences of your material, your corrections and readings, and (in a session) your explanation and answers. Temperature is 0.2. With reasoning `none` it adds `reasoning_effort: "none"` and `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`; with reply shape `server` it adds a `response_format` with the reply's JSON Schema.

headers.Authorization: `Bearer <key>`, only when settings name an API key variable (`apiKeyEnv`).

GET {baseURL}/models.description: Lists the models a server has, to check that the answer model and the meaning-search model are installed. Sent once per server address each time the Today or Settings page loads, and by the `kizuki` command at start. Gives up after 5 seconds. Carries no study data.

headers.Authorization: `Bearer <key>`, only when settings name an API key variable (`apiKeyEnv`). The key is read from that environment variable.
